issues.description: compile_notebook RPC contract silently broadened to ship full script content over the wire
issues.detail: The RPC's postcondition was a small metadata envelope. Adding script_content changes the contract: callers now receive arbitrary-size file contents on every compile. No precondition limits size, no spec states the field is optional, and existing callers were not part of the decision. State the new contract explicitly or expose a separate read_script(path) operation that callers invoke on demand.

issues.description: DeployProgress conflates two abstractions: progress display and file-download mechanics
issues.detail: The component's ADT is 'render deploy progress.' handleDownloadClick now embeds Blob construction, object URLs, DOM manipulation, and revoke lifecycle. That is a separate abstraction (a downloader). Extract a downloadFile(name, content) utility so the component's contract stays 'render state' and the download mechanism is substitutable and testable in isolation.

issues.description: Download affordance precondition unenforced at the type level
issues.detail: The button is rendered unconditionally in the success branch, but handleDownloadClick guards on both compiledPath and compiledContent. If compiledContent is ever undefined (older backend, error path, future caller), the click is a silent no-op — a weakened postcondition for the user. Either make compiledContent required in this branch's type, or hide the icon when absent.

issues.description: compiledContent field added to DeployProgressState without spec or lifetime contract
issues.detail: The state type gains compiledContent: string with no documented invariant — when is it set, when cleared, what bounds its size, who owns disposal. For a long-lived multi-component state object this is the spot to write the contract, otherwise future maintainers will guess. A short JSDoc on the field stating 'present iff compile succeeded; raw .kale.py source' would suffice.

issues.description: Script file read without encoding specification leaks platform behavior through the contract
issues.detail: open(script_path) uses the platform default encoding. The RPC's postcondition for script_content is therefore platform-dependent — a leak of implementation through the interface. Specify open(script_path, encoding='utf-8') so the returned string has a stated contract independent of the server's locale.

review.summary: The change implements a reasonable feature but quietly amends two contracts without stating them: the compile_notebook RPC now returns arbitrary-size file content as a side product of compilation, and DeployProgressState gains a field with no documented lifetime. The DeployProgress component also absorbs file-download mechanics that belong in a separate abstraction, weakening its ADT (render progress) by complecting it with browser DOM plumbing. None of this is catastrophic, but for a long-lived multi-team Jupyter extension the right move is to name the contracts: make compiledContent's presence a precondition of rendering the button, extract a download utility, and either fix the encoding or expose a dedicated read-script RPC.
